name: Mila Vidaković — The Witness

choices: Look at the car and the people in it — try to see the Duchess's face before the crowd blocks your view
Look at the young man at the corner — the one who has not moved since the car stopped
Look at the crowd around you — see how they are reacting to the car's unexpected stop
opening.narrative: The crowd around you is three and four deep at the curb, thinner where you are, pressed back against the shop fronts. The morning smells of wool and chestnut smoke and the faint mineral cold of the river. Somewhere above you a window opens and a woman leans out with a small Austro-Hungarian flag. The engine noise of the motorcade is growing louder from the direction of the Town Hall — you can hear it over the brass band, a low mechanical rumble that the crowd recognizes and responds to with a surge forward, a collective leaning toward the road. The great open car swings onto Franz Josef Street. It is moving too fast for the narrow turn. Then it is not moving at all.

briefing: Your shoulders are pressed against the cold limestone of Schiller's shop window and you have been standing here for nearly two hours. You came early to get a good position — close enough to see the Duchess's face, close enough to wave your handkerchief and have it perhaps seen — and the crowd has filled in around you until there is no comfortable way to stand. The child to your left has been on her father's shoulders since nine o'clock and is beginning to droop. The brass band on the quay has been playing the same three pieces in rotation. You heard something earlier — a flat crack from the direction of the river, then a sound like a cart overturning, and people running, and then the cheering resuming as if nothing had happened, which confused you. The motorcade is coming back now; you can hear the engine noise growing from the direction of the Town Hall, and the crowd around you is pressing forward, handkerchiefs out, the child above you suddenly awake and waving. Then the great open car swings onto your street, and something is wrong with the way it is moving.
description: You came to see the Duchess's gown and wave a handkerchief on a Sunday morning. You are about to see something else entirely — something you will spend the rest of your life trying to describe accurately.
perspective: Write from the perspective of an ordinary civilian with no special knowledge, no authority, and no power over events — a person whose entire role is the quality and precision of her witnessing. She notices small things: the color of a pennant, the sound a car makes when it stalls, the angle of a young man's arm. Her experience is the rupture of a festive Sunday morning into something that has no name yet.
character_hooks: I live two streets from here — I have walked past Schiller's corner a thousand times, and I know exactly how narrow the turn is from the quay.
My brother told me this morning not to stand too close to the road after what happened with the bomb — I moved back to the shop window specifically because of what he said.

I was watching the young man at the corner before the car arrived — there was something about the way he was standing, very still, not looking at the motorcade, that I noticed and then forgot about until the car stopped.
context_sentence: You are Mila Vidaković, a woman pressed against a shop window with a handkerchief in your fist, and the Archduke's car has stopped directly in front of you.

inventory: Sunday coat — good wool, slightly too warm for the morning

startingKnowledge: That a bomb or grenade was thrown at the motorcade earlier this morning — you heard the explosion from the direction of the quay
That the motorcade is returning from the Town Hall and will pass along the Appel Quay
The face of the young man standing at the corner of Schiller's shop — you noticed him because he was not cheering
